title: Rebuilding his reputation with Elaine's help
summary: As an ex-addict with a bad reputation he started over with scale gigs and settled in the mountains.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: club date player or a jazz player in New York and you were never--
Yeah, I had to-- you know, during all the drug years, I developed a reputation of being, number one, a junkie, number two, undependable and number three, untrustworthy.

When I finally settled with the drug problem, kicked that in the ass, I discovered that I had to start all over from the very beginning. Telephones wouldn't answer to me, people weren't in to me and this was pretty much warranted. I earned it by being untrustworthy, undependable and an addict, and so I started from the beginning.

I went back rejoined the union, met Elaine, which was the major factor in my being as successful as I've been up to this point, in coming back, in coming back to life. But I had to do it by going out to Staten Island on Saturday nights and working in a little, dingy joint under scale, and I had a day job as a messenger

delivering packages, making forty three dollars a week that way, but it was all important, all very important. It was a way of me beginning to believe in myself that I was a man, that I could be depended on, be responsible.
Was there a feeling then that with some work we can wipe this all aside and be back where we were?

I just felt that there was no reason to look back, that I had something to do and I had better get about doing it, and I had a beautiful old lady who was standing right there with me; the most help to me.

I started to work more and more, showed up on time, showed up clean, I performed properly, I did a better than average job, started to become recommended again, and this took me to the point where I told you I came up here to take a job as a pianist in the mountains playing in a showband, and I stayed up here for a while by myself; Elaine was down in the city and would come up on weekends and she fell in
love with the place up here and we decided to settle here and leave the city.

Through the years we rented a cottage and we rented a bungalow and finally bought our own place, and we've been here about ten years, and as I told you before, we're still not unpacked. I can see what we have to do with this house yet, but we're building.
Not being unpacked, I gather signals you really want to go back to the city?

No, no. There's so much to build here and what isn't unpacked yet, are our books. We have to build a bookcase; it's going to go right around that area, around the windows. Then we'll be completely unpacked.
